court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
trial_court: Additional Principal Judge Family Court, Pilibhit, Execution Case No. 9 of 2022 (Smt. Neeraj Saini Vs. Ankit Suman)
case_name: Ankit Suman vs State Of U.P. And Another

parties.respondent_defendant: State of U.P. and Another, wife

facts_of_case: The husband-petitioner filed a petition for divorce from his wife-respondent under Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. The respondent-wife appeared and filed a written statement denying the allegations made by the petitioner. During pendency of this petition, an application under Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act was filed by the respondent-wife to which the petitioner filed objections.

legal_principles.principle: Proceeding in a suit commences with the filing of the plaint.
legal_principles.held: On the plaint being filed, summons is issued to the defendant, who on its service appears in the Court and files his written statement.
cited_cases: Amrit Lal Nehru Vs. Usha Nehru (1982) J&K 98
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — significance in understanding the commencement of a suit

legal_principles.principle: The word 'during the proceedings' under Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 are of great consequence.
legal_principles.held: This term would cover the proceedings from the start till end to at least from the date the application is made till the termination of proceedings in the Court.
cited_cases: Amrit Lal Nehru Vs. Usha Nehru (1982) J&K 98
legal_principles.significance: MEDIUM — importance in understanding the scope of Section 24

outcome.final_order: The order dated 30.10.2020 passed by Additional Principal Judge Family Court, Pilibhit was set aside and the application filed by respondent No. 2 under Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act was allowed.
